classificationRule: Publication supports qualitative direction only unless explicit quotation says otherwise. All gameplay coefficients and continuous mappings are tuning; no automatic2D port.

sources.title: CDC: Symptoms of Mild TBI and Concussion
sources.limits: SCAT5 BJSM PDF returned429 and CISG mirror403. Symptom list corroborated with CDC; no claim of reading the blocked SCAT5 PDF. Focus-lag waveform, strength and duration are tuning.

sources.title: Theodoroff et al.: Concussion Management Guidelines Neglect Auditory Symptoms. DOI10.1097/JSM.0000000000000874
verifiedQuotes: Tinnitus, noise sensitivity, and hearing difficulties are commonly reported secondary to head injury.
sources.limits: Supports tinnitus/noise sensitivity after head injury; symptom risk-to-gain mapping and120s decay are tuning. Reuses v46 oscillator/gain, does not create a second tone.

sources.title: Joyner & Casey2015: Regulation of increased blood flow (hyperemia) to muscles during exercise. DOI10.1152/physrev.00035.2013
verifiedQuotes: At rest, cardiac output is ∼5 l/min and rises to ∼20 l/min in the untrained subject during maximum exercise.
renal and splanchnic blood flow can both fall to ∼25% of resting values during heavy exercise in humans
oxygen consumption in these tissues is preserved by marked increases in extraction
sources.limits: Untrained maximum approximately5→20L/min is context for tuning target3–4x. Not a prediction for a particular loaded soldier. Organ factor1/(1+4I) multiplies current CO, not a direct claim that final organ flow equals25% of rest. Oxygen extraction, preload^4, pump/HR constants are tuning.

sources.title: Heart-rate recovery immediately after exercise as a predictor of mortality. DOI10.1056/NEJM199910283411804
sources.access: Europe PMC bibliographic record and original abstract verified
verifiedQuotes: Recovery of the heart rate immediately after exercise is a function of vagal reactivation.
The value for the recovery of heart rate was defined as the decrease in the heart rate from peak exercise to one minute after the cessation of exercise.
An abnormal value ... 12 beats per minute or less
sources.limits: 12bpm is a cohort/protocol prognostic cut point, not a universal recovery curve. Rise18s/recovery45s time constants and150–180bpm loaded run target are tuning, not Cole measurements.

sources.title: Rohmert1960: Ermittlung von Erholungspausen für statische Arbeit des Menschen
sources.access: Original bibliographic record verified; no original curve/table text obtained
sources.limits: No original Rohmert coefficients copied. MVC→time log-interpolated anchors are a game-authored monotone endurance approximation, not a digitized1960 curve.40Nm shoulder reference and lever arms are tuning.

sources.title: Pulling strength, muscular fatigue, and prediction of maximum endurance time for simulated pulling tasks2018
sources.limits: Supports load fraction/endurance dependence and posture specificity, not transfer of measured pulling durations to rifle holding. The entire rifle endurance curve remains tuning. Exact1960 curve shape not independently reproduced.
verifiedParaphrases: Rohmert posture-specific models compared; posture5 employed muscles on back/hip and lower limbs.
Models differ with recruited muscle groups/posture.
